title: PSY 361 — Exam 3: Personality
subject: Psychology 101
description: Chapters 5 & 6: self-concept, self-esteem, Freud, defense mechanisms, Jung, Adler, Horney. 46 questions across 4 rounds.

rounds.title: Warm-Up: The Self
rounds.desc: Chapter 5 — self-concept, self-esteem, self-efficacy, self-regulation. Lock in the foundations.

rounds.title: Freud & Defense Mechanisms
rounds.desc: Id/ego/superego, psychosexual stages, and scenario-style defense mechanism questions — classic exam traps.

rounds.title: Scholar vs Scholar
rounds.desc: Where exam points live. Freud vs Jung vs Adler vs Horney — prove you know where the theorists disagree.

rounds.title: Closing the Gaps
rounds.desc: Everything the first three rounds didn't cover — imposter syndrome, psychosexual stage details, transference, object-relations names, and more.

questions.q: Your self-concept is best described as…
options: The cognitive structure (schema) that organizes knowledge about yourself
Your overall positive or negative evaluation of yourself
Your ability to override impulses for long-term goals
The social mask you wear around others
questions.explain: Self-concept = the schema. The evaluation part is self-esteem.

questions.q: In William James's terms, the “I” is…
options: The active perceiver — the self doing the thinking
The self as an object being observed and evaluated
The self defined by social roles
questions.explain: “I” = the thinker. “Me” = the self being observed and evaluated.

questions.q: Body, clothing, possessions, home — which “self” (James)?
questions.explain: Material self = physical aspects: body, clothing, possessions, home.

questions.q: Self-esteem is…
options: Your overall positive or negative evaluation of yourself
Your belief you can perform a specific task
Adjusting your behavior to fit social situations
Treating yourself kindly when you fail
questions.explain: Task-specific belief = self-efficacy. Adjusting behavior = self-monitoring.

questions.q: Leary's sociometer theory says self-esteem works as…
options: An internal gauge of social acceptance vs. rejection
A fixed trait set in childhood
A direct cause of life success
questions.explain: It drops when you sense exclusion — a social meter, not a success engine. Correlation ≠ causation.

questions.q: “I believe I can nail this specific presentation” — that's…
questions.explain: Self-efficacy (Bandura) = belief about SPECIFIC tasks. Self-esteem is global.

questions.q: Self-efficacy is built by all of these EXCEPT…
questions.explain: Bandura's four builders: mastery experiences, vicarious learning, verbal persuasion, managing arousal.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of Neff's three parts of self-compassion?
questions.explain: Neff: self-kindness (not self-judgment), common humanity, mindfulness.

questions.q: Self-regulation vs. self-control:
options: Regulation is the broad process; control is the narrow subset of overriding impulses
They mean exactly the same thing
Control is broad; regulation is narrow
Regulation is unconscious; control is conscious
questions.explain: Self-control = the narrow subset: overriding immediate temptations for long-term goals.

questions.q: Higgins: actual-vs-ideal mismatch → ?  Actual-vs-ought mismatch → ?
questions.explain: Ideal = hopes (missing them = dejection). Ought = duties (missing them = agitation).

questions.q: Id, ego, superego run on which principles, in order?
questions.explain: Id = pleasure principle, ego = reality principle, superego = morals and conscience.

questions.q: Topographical vs. structural model:
options: Topographical = levels of awareness; structural = parts of personality
Structural = levels of awareness; topographical = parts of personality
questions.explain: Classic exam trap: topographical = WHERE in the mind; structural = WHO is fighting.

questions.q: After a brutal performance review, Maya goes home and yells at her roommate. Defense?
questions.explain: Displacement = redirecting feelings from the real target to a safer one.

questions.q: Leo is attracted to his coworker but loudly insists she's “disgusting.” Defense?
questions.explain: Reaction formation = expressing the exact OPPOSITE of a forbidden impulse.

questions.q: Nina cheated on the exam but accuses her study partner of cheating. Defense?
questions.explain: Projection = attributing YOUR unacceptable impulse to someone else.

questions.q: Carlos channels his aggression into competitive boxing. Defense?
questions.explain: Sublimation = channeling forbidden drives into socially valued activity.

questions.q: Refusing to accept an unpleasant reality (“I'm not sick, the test is wrong”):
questions.explain: Denial = refusing the reality. Repression pushes it fully out of awareness.

questions.q: The remembered storyline and images of a dream — the surface level:
questions.explain: Manifest = surface story. Latent = the hidden unconscious meaning underneath.

questions.q: Harsh toilet training → adult who is orderly, stingy, stubborn. Which fixation?
questions.explain: Harsh training → anal-retentive. Lax training → anal-expulsive (messy, rebellious).

questions.q: Which is NOT a standard criticism of Freud's theory?
options: He relied too heavily on laboratory experiments
He built theory on unrepresentative case studies
questions.explain: Freud famously did NOT run lab experiments — that's the opposite of the real criticisms.

questions.q: Who said the unconscious includes a shared COLLECTIVE layer stocked with archetypes?
questions.explain: Jung's big break from Freud: the collective unconscious, inherited universal patterns.

questions.q: Freud vs. Jung on “libido”:
options: Freud = sexual energy; Jung = general psychic life-energy
Jung = sexual energy; Freud = general psychic life-energy
questions.explain: This exact disagreement is what SPLIT them.

questions.q: “Striving for superiority” as the core human motive — whose idea?
questions.explain: Adler: not sex, but social striving to overcome inferiority.

questions.q: Who fired back at “penis envy” with “womb envy”?
questions.explain: Horney argued culture — a male-dominated society — not anatomy, explains women's psychology.

questions.q: Freud reads dreams BACKWARD (past forbidden wishes). Jung reads them…
options: Forward — compensating the conscious attitude, pointing at growth
questions.explain: Jung: dreams are compensatory and prospective — they balance your conscious attitude.

questions.q: “Basic anxiety” — a child feeling isolated and helpless in a hostile world. Whose concept?
questions.explain: Horney's core problem. Her fix = three coping styles: toward, against, away.

questions.q: Coping by moving TOWARD, AGAINST, or AWAY from people — whose neurotic styles?
questions.explain: Horney: toward = compliance, against = aggression/dominance, away = detachment.

questions.q: Individuation — integrating the shadow into a whole Self. Whose goal of development?
questions.explain: Jung's goal. Freud's = make the unconscious conscious. Adler's = build social interest.

questions.q: Birth order shaping personality (firstborns responsible, middles competitive) — whose idea?
questions.explain: Adler tied ordinal position to personality patterns.

questions.q: The goal of Freudian therapy:
questions.explain: Freud: insight via free association and dream analysis. Individuation = Jung. Social interest = Adler.

questions.q: Despite straight A's, Jordan is convinced he's a fraud who'll be exposed any day. That's…
questions.explain: Imposter phenomenon = doubting your accomplishments and fearing exposure despite evidence of competence.

questions.q: After his team wins, Marcus keeps saying “WE won the championship.” That's…
questions.explain: BIRGing = boosting self-esteem by associating with others' successes.

questions.q: Per the self-evaluation maintenance (SEM) model, when your close friend beats you at something that matters deeply to you, you tend to…
questions.explain: SEM: bask when they win where it DOESN'T matter to you; distance when they beat you where it DOES.

questions.q: Explicit vs. implicit self-esteem:
options: Explicit = conscious self-evaluation; implicit = automatic, unconscious
Both are measured only by brain scans
questions.explain: Explicit = deliberate self-reports. Implicit = automatic, gut-level evaluation.

questions.q: The “causation trap” in self-esteem research means…
options: High self-esteem correlates with good outcomes, but boosting it doesn't cause success
Low self-esteem is always caused by parents
questions.explain: Correlation ≠ causation — a favorite exam trap.

questions.q: “Possible selves” are…
options: Mental images of who you might become, hope to become, or fear becoming
Your past selves that you regret
The masks you wear in social situations
questions.explain: Possible selves motivate behavior — feared selves push you away, hoped-for selves pull you forward.

questions.q: Transference is when…
options: A patient redirects feelings from early relationships onto the therapist
The therapist falls asleep during sessions
Memories move from short- to long-term storage
A dream's latent content becomes manifest
questions.explain: Transference = unconsciously redirecting early-relationship feelings onto the therapist.

questions.q: Free association means…
options: Saying whatever comes to mind uncensored, to surface unconscious material
A dream technique using fixed symbols
questions.explain: Freud's 'talking cure' tool: uncensored speech surfaces unconscious material.

questions.q: Fixation at the oral stage (birth–18 months) can produce an adult who is…
options: Dependent, prone to smoking or overeating
questions.explain: Oral = mouth pleasure (sucking/biting). Orderly/stingy = anal-retentive; messy/rebellious = anal-expulsive.

questions.q: In the phallic stage, the Oedipus complex resolves when the boy…
options: Identifies with his father (driven by castration anxiety)
Skips straight to the genital stage
questions.explain: Boy desires mother, rivals father; castration anxiety drives identification with father.

questions.q: During the latency stage, libido is…
options: Dormant — energy goes to school, friends, and skills
questions.explain: Latency (~6 to puberty): sexual energy quiets; focus shifts to school and peers.

questions.q: “Day residue” refers to…
options: Recent waking experiences woven into dream imagery
The hidden meaning of a dream
Psychic energy invested in an idea
questions.explain: Day residue = yesterday's experiences showing up in tonight's dream imagery.

questions.q: Cathexis is…
options: Investing psychic energy in a person, object, or idea
questions.explain: Cathexis = where you 'put' your libido — your psychic energy's target.

questions.q: Match the object-relations theorist — “splitting” (seeing people as all-good or all-bad):
questions.explain: Klein = splitting. Winnicott = good-enough mother, transitional objects. Mahler = separation-individuation.

questions.q: The Persona vs. the Shadow (Jung):
options: Persona = social mask; Shadow = dark hidden self
Persona = hidden self; Shadow = social mask
Both live only in the personal unconscious
questions.explain: Persona = the face you show the world. Shadow = the dark parts you hide — individuation integrates it.

questions.q: Adler's “social interest” means…
options: Healthy adjustment = caring about the community, not just yourself
Preferring group study over solo study
questions.explain: For Adler, mental health = contributing to the community, not just overcoming inferiority for yourself.
